title: Five seconds slow after two months at sea: how John Harrison's H4 found longitude

posts.facebook:
A self-taught carpenter, a watch that ticked five times a second, and decades spent finding a ship's place at sea.

How John Harrison, a self-taught clockmaker, built the four marine timekeepers H1 to H4, how H4 performed on the voyages to Jamaica and Barbados, why the Board of Longitude hesitated, what he was paid, and where the accounts differ.

A breakthrough is only half the work: proving it, and persuading the people who must accept it, can take as long again.

Read the full story → https://dontdieretired.com/curious/john-harrison-h4-longitude/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=daily
